glosses: To mash; to crush (usually food) into a smooth substance.

examples.text: mash up the avocados
mash up the pills

glosses: To disfigure, devastate or destroy.

examples.text: The car accident mashed up my legs, now I'm never going to walk again.

glosses: To remix two or more songs together into one.

examples.text: The DJ mashed up Britney Spears and Daft Punk.

glosses: A sport played in a walled court with a soft rubber ball and bats like tennis racquets.

examples.text: She plays squash every Saturday.

Ivor had acquired more than a mile of fishing rights with the house; he was not at all a good fisherman, but one must do something; one generally, however, banged a ball with a squash-racket against a wall.

glosses: A non-alcoholic drink made from a fruit-based concentrate diluted with water or milk.

examples.text: Sure. I pour hot squash all over myself and we all have a good chuckle. Everyone except Muggins here.
When I'm thirsty I drink squash; it tastes much nicer than plain water.

glosses: A place or a situation where people have limited space to move.

examples.text: It's a bit of a squash in this small room.

glosses: A preparation made by placing material on a slide (flat, rectangular piece of glass), covering it and applying pressure.
Something soft and easily crushed; especially, an unripe pod of peas.
Something unripe or soft.
A sudden fall of a heavy, soft body; also, a shock of soft bodies.
An extremely one-sided, usually short, match.

examples.text: It was one of the most shocking WWE title matches ever witnessed, and effectively a 20-minute squash match as Brock Lesnar "conquered" his opponent.

glosses: To beat or press into pulp or a flat mass; to crush.
To compress or restrict (oneself) into a small space; to squeeze.

examples.text: Somehow, she squashed all her books into her backpack, which was now too heavy to carry.
We all managed to squash into Mum's tiny car.

glosses: To suppress; to force into submission.

examples.text: A somewhat popular myth about the Whiskey Rebellion is that Washington personally led the troops into western Pennsylvania and squashed the rebellion.

glosses: The sound of something relatively heavy splashing or squelching into water.

examples.text: […] rain, too, had lately fallen, and had decidedly not evaporated, since, at every step, I went squash! squash! up to the tops of my boots, and many times very extent, stretching to the eastward, […]
[…] to catch all the rain […]; my boots went squash, squash, as I turned on to the high road, […]

1883, May 5 […] The words had only left his mouth when his feet slipped from under him, and with a dull, sickening thud, he went squash! into the water, waist-deep. We made our way to bed in a silence that was painful.

glosses: The sound or action of something, especially something moist, being squeezed or crushed.

examples.text: Alex reached the bottom and Grant heard a squish as she landed in the mud on the bottom of the river.

glosses: A political moderate.

examples.text: Some conservatives think that in the long run, the party will be better off without squishes like Specter […]

“Josh Mandel: Another failed career politician squish,” a new ad from a super PAC supporting Mr. Vance blared on Ohio television sets on Friday, calling Mr. Mandel, who is mounting his third Senate run, a “two-time loser” and “a moderate for the moderates.”

glosses: Marmalade.

examples.text: Where they are loaves and joints melt as snow in the sunshine; bowls of cream are of no more account than acorn-cups filled with dew; and the 'squish'—as they call the mother's home-made marmalade—has to be renewed daily; […]

There was a time when the “squish” manufactured by Mr. Frank Cooper at Oxford was not known very extensively outside the world of undergraduates. With the march of events though the fame of Cooper's Oxford marmalade has become world-wide, and the natural consequence is that a new factory has had to be built to cope with the increased business.

glosses: To squeeze, compress, or crush (especially something moist).

examples.text: The sandwich tasted fine, even though it had got squished in his lunchbox.
Rather than squishing everything into a tiny window, I have shown only part of my app.

glosses: To be compressed or squeezed.

examples.text: I kicked off my shoes and wiggled my toes on the soft moss. It felt amazing as it squished between my toes, […]

glosses: A non-romantic and generally non-sexual infatuation with somebody one is not dating, or the object of that infatuation; a platonic crush.

examples.text: Sur l’ordre du commodore Cartwright, les canons furent prêts à canonner. Du haut d’un petit mur, le jeune homme écrabouilla à coups de serpe la tête d’une truie. Celle-là était sauvage et se ruait sur l’homme comme un taureau. Elle avait mangé ses porcelets.
Et je ne te dis rien des fois où vous nous tapiez sur la gueule avec vos monstres de canons au lieu d’écrabouiller les Boches…
Idéalement, en démocratie, on devrait avoir envie d’utiliser le formidable pouvoir de la communication pour faire bouger les mentalités au lieu de les écrabouiller.
